```python
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("Transportation_Problem")
    m.setParam("TimeLimit", 300)  # Set time limit to 300 seconds

    # Data
    sources = list(range(10))  # S0..S9
    destinations = list(range(13))  # D0..D12

    supplies = [52, 53, 73, 83, 65, 91, 91, 27, 68, 55]
    demands = [44, 33, 72, 65, 16, 56, 41, 43, 28, 60, 47, 67, 21]

    # Cost matrix: rows correspond to sources S0..S9, columns to destinations D0..D12
    costs = [
        [ 11.82,  14.20,  25.96,  23.62,  16.40,  27.11,  23.96,  26.74,   8.89,  23.61,  28.41,  15.77,  16.73],  # S0
        [ 15.28,   7.49,  29.95,  17.44,  28.37,   9.76,  15.06,  24.87,  18.40,  14.85,  16.22,  14.70,  15.79],  # S1
        [ 13.30,  15.97,  12.06,  27.20,  16.70,  12.34,  21.49,  25.14,  12.47,  27.05,  19.42,  21.74,  17.29],  # S2
        [ 13.19,   7.60,   7.56,   9.21,  29.17,   9.78,   8.38,  29.73,  18.84,  13.12,   9.55,  16.68,  12.79],  # S3
        [ 18.77,   7.23,  11.41,  14.67,  22.24,  15.27,  27.12,  19.41,   9.24,  20.26,  27.96,  22.06,  24.49],  # S4
        [ 23.42,   6.16,  19.64,  19.63,  18.34,  19.27,  21.40,  19.36,   8.01,  24.25,  26.55,  28.24,  24.42],  # S5
        [ 13.94,  29.28,  24.97,  24.02,   9.13,  20.19,   8.28,  24.23,  13.26,  20.50,  13.16,  12.56,  10.90],  # S6
        [  9.44,  13.51,  20.01,  11.78,   9.03,  22.30,  12.91,  13.75,  16.65,  28.90,  15.90,  23.58,  22.06],  # S7
        [ 10.29,  14.73,  17.16,  12.39,  22.76,  23.36,  15.28,  25.42,  26.13,  25.63,  22.76,   8.44,  21.77],  # S8
        [ 15.15,  29.88,   5.63,  28.66,  10.47,  26.29,  28.19,   9.59,  25.12,  20.68,  25.80,  14.24,  16.88],  # S9
    ]

    # Decision variables:
    # Flow_S{i}_D{j} >= 0 is the quantity shipped from source i to destination j
    flows = {}
    for i in sources:
        for j in destinations:
            flows[(i, j)] = m.addVar(lb=0.0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Flow_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Objective: Minimize total transportation cost
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(costs[i][j] * flows[(i, j)] for i in sources for j in destinations),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # Supply constraints: Shipments from each source <= its supply
    for i in sources:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(flows[(i, j)] for j in destinations) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}"
        )

    # Demand constraints: Shipments to each destination >= its demand
    for j in destinations:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(flows[(i, j)] for i in sources) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}"
        )

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Subject: Network shipping plan to meet demand at the lowest cost
Date: [Date]

Situation:
Our network includes multiple source locations (warehouses and factories) supplying multiple destination locations (stores and customers). Customer service levels and freight spend are sensitive to how we allocate shipments across routes. Partial shipments are allowed, which gives us flexibility to split orders across lanes when it reduces cost or improves service.

Problem:
Shipping costs vary by route, each source has limited inventory, and each destination has a required quantity to receive. Without a coordinated, data-driven plan, we risk stock imbalances, missed deliveries, and avoidable transportation expense. We need a clear allocation of shipments from each source to each destination that:
- Does not exceed available inventory at any source
- Meets the required quantity at every destination
- Achieves the lowest total transportation cost across the network

Approach:
- Confirm the latest supply availability, destination requirements, and route-level shipping costs.
- Develop a consolidated shipment allocation plan that leverages partial shipments where beneficial.
- Validate feasibility with operations (lead times, dock capacity, carrier commitments, cut-off times).
- Publish the recommended source-to-destination plan, with route assignments and an estimated cost summary.
- Monitor execution and adjust as conditions change (inventory updates, demand shifts, carrier constraints).

Expected outcome:
A practical shipping plan that meets all demand requirements, stays within available inventory, and reduces overall freight spend while maintaining service levels.
